canonical_name: Weyl dimension formula for irreducible compact Lie-group representations (exact domain and convention open)
literal_source_claim_zh: 紧李群不可约表示的维数
literal_source_claim_en: Dimensions of irreducible representations of compact Lie groups.
statement_blocker: The catalog does not fix connectedness or reductivity, representation field and continuity, maximal torus, positive-root system, highest-weight and dominance conventions, roots versus coroots, Weyl-vector and pairing normalization, product codomain and coercions, denominator nonvanishing, or central, torus, disconnected, and empty-root cases. The 1925 Weyl paper is only a bibliographic lead and no exact lawful source passage has been crosswalked. Freezing the familiar product from memory would invent the missing theorem boundary.
domain_and_universes: Open: an approved source must fix the compact group class and topology, connectedness and reductivity, maximal torus and root-data carriers, scalar field, representation carrier and universes, finite-dimensionality and continuity, weight and coweight lattices, and all typeclass assumptions.
conclusion: Prospective family only: the finite dimension of a source-selected irreducible representation equals a source-normalized product indexed by positive roots and determined by its dominant highest weight. The exact equality, factors, scalar codomain, coercions, and representation-to-weight correspondence remain open.
degenerate_case_status: No case is excluded before a proposition is selected; the statement phase must resolve the trivial group, tori and centers, disconnected groups, rank zero, empty roots and products, trivial and invalid weights, reducible and zero-dimensional representations, denominator nonvanishing, positive-system independence, isogenies, and scalar-field conventions.
candidate_scope_not_credited: the classical highest-weight product formula for a compact connected semisimple Lie group
a compact connected reductive variant separating the central torus
the corresponding finite-dimensional semisimple complex Lie-algebra highest-weight formula
a specialization or limit of the Weyl character formula at the identity
root-system-level product formulas after independently supplying the representation-to-highest-weight bridge
excluded_substitutions: the Weyl character formula without a checked identity specialization or limiting transport
the highest-weight classification theorem without the numerical product identity
the Weyl denominator identity, Weyl integration formula, Weyl law, or Weyl-group order
finite-group character dimension facts or character orthogonality
an abstract positive-root product detached from an irreducible representation and its highest weight
a rank-one, SU(2), classical-family, symmetric-power, or other special-case calculation
a structure, field, hypothesis, table, or computation storing the requested equality
the catalog's untrusted verified label, a theorem-name match, generic infrastructure, or the intake probe used as proof credit
